newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan aims to cut group assets to 170 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan aims to cut group assets to 170 bln yen.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp said on Monday that it aims to cut group assets to 170 billion yen by the end of March 1999 from 249.4 billion yen as of the end of March 1996.
It also plans to reduce group debt subject to interest payments to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen, the company said in a statement.
Yaohan Japan, the flagship firm of the international retail group, also plans to sell more than 10 stores and offices in the next two years, the statement said.
In December, the company said that it would implement several restructuring measures to prop up its business.
Earlier that same month, the company asked its 477 suppliers if it could extend the time-lag between merchandise delivery and payment to two months from one month.

The company also aims to reduce parent assets to 120 billion yen by the end of March 1999 from 178.9 billion yen as of the end of March 1996, while cutting interest-bearing parent debts to 60 billion yen from 101.8 billion yen.
The company also plans to sell part of its stock holdings and assets in Japan and abroad.
It also plans to obtain loans from financial institutions to pay holders of its maturing corporate bonds, the statement said.
